newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks trail Dow higher at open.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks trail Dow higher at open.

text.p: The Australian share market trailed a strong Wall Street higher at the open on Monday but with a weaker gold sector dragging on the market.
From the opening, the All Ordinaries index added 14.9 points to 2,414.4.
Brokers said solid gains by the leaders had taken the market ahead, overcoming a gold index that dived more than one percent after the bullion price tumbled to three-year lows in overseas markets.
"The Dow's gone ahead again and I'm expecting reasonable if unspectacular gains today," said a Sydney-based dealer.
Industrials and resources saw the gains fairly evenly shared with the weaker gold sector not enough to prevent the resources group moving ahead.

Featuring early was retailer David Jones whose shares continued to slide after Friday's warning of a 50-percent cut in first-half profit forecasts because of depressed retail trading conditions. David Jones shares slid over six percent to A$1.56 (US$1.23).

Against the trend in the gold sector was situation stock Highlands Gold which unveiled restructuring plans to fend off a hostile bid from gold major Placer Dome. Highlands shares jumped over five percent to A$0.79.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about eight to five, while about 33 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
